fields.Participants: Sales Rep, AR Clerk, AR Supervisor, Finance Manager, Credit Committee
fields.Trigger: Customer applies for trade or corporate credit account

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-submit of "submits credit application" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "AR Clerk runs credit check" (replaces manual Step 3).
- System auto-generate of "prepares credit assessment with recommended limit and terms" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - CTL-12 (separate credit approval from sales execution.); CTL-43 (prevent Sales Rep self-approval of credit limits on own accounts.)
- operational: AR Supervisor review and approval gate
Credit Approval Matrix: | > PHP 1,000,000 | Credit Committee (CFO + Finance Manager + AR Supervisor) |
Pain Points / Risks: - **Insufficient credit bureau infrastructure in the Philippines**: unlike mature markets, Philippine credit bureaus (CIC, TransUnion) have limited coverage for SME trade accounts; credit assessment relies heavily on trade references and bank certification letters, which can be fabricated or from related parties

- **Credit limit override pressure from Sales Reps**: during promotional periods or large project orders, Sales Reps pressure AR Supervisors to approve higher credit limits beyond what the assessment supports; ad-hoc limit increases without proper assessment increase bad debt exposure (W81)

- **Annual credit review backlog**: with ~5,200 active accounts, reviewing each annually at 5 min/account = ~433 hours/year; AR Clerks often deprioritize credit reviews in favor of urgent collections work, leaving some accounts with outdated credit limits that no longer reflect the customer's financial condition

- **Corporate account concentration risk**: ~200 corporate accounts may represent a disproportionate share of AR exposure; a single large corporate account default (e.g., a major construction company) could exceed PHP 10M, dwarfing the combined exposure of hundreds of smaller trade accounts; mitigated by CTL-12 (separate credit approval from sales execution.); CTL-43 (prevent Sales Rep self-approval of credit limits on own accounts)
Staffing Implication: - **AR Clerks** (3–4): 100–150 applications/month × ~90 min each = 150–225 hours/month. Spread across 3–4 clerks = ~50 hours/clerk/month. Absorbed within existing AR team workload, primarily in the first half of the month when collection activity is lighter.
System Touchpoints: - Credit application form (online or in-store) (W24.1)
- Customer master creation with credit limit, payment terms, entity assignment, and VAT treatment classification (W24.6)

- VAT treatment per customer account: AR Clerk classifies account as Standard (12% VAT), VAT-Exempt (government agencies with BIR ruling, PEZA-registered entities), or Zero-Rated (export sales) during account setup based on supporting documents (BIR ruling, PEZA certificate, government purchase order, diplomatic note); system stores VAT treatment in customer master; applied automatically at POS (W5B.4c) and AR invoicing (W8) (W24.6)
- Credit limit enforcement at POS/sales order (W24.6 → W8.3)
- Annual credit review scheduling and workflow (W24.8)
Time Estimate: - Credit application processing: ~90 min/application (verification + credit check + assessment)
- Monthly volume: 100–150 applications × 90 min = ~150–225 hours/month
- Approval per tier: ~10–30 min/application
- Account creation and activation: ~25 min/application
- Annual credit review: ~5 min/account × ~5,200 accounts (system-generated tickler with 20–30 min manual depth only on flagged accounts per W1300) = ~433 system hours + ~500–800 manual hours/year
- Total credit processing: ~200–275 hours/month across 3–4 AR Clerks

steps.activity: Customer submits credit application (in-store, via Sales Rep, or online form)
AR Clerk verifies application completeness: business registration, financial statements, trade references
AR Clerk runs credit check (bank references, trade references, external credit bureau if available)
AR Clerk prepares credit assessment with recommended limit and terms
Approval per tier (see matrix below)
System creates customer account with approved credit limit, payment terms, and entity assignment
Customer notified of approval; account activated
Annual credit review: AR Clerk reviews all accounts for limit adjustment (increase, decrease, or suspension)

fields.Frequency: Daily collection activities; weekly escalation review; monthly portfolio review
fields.Owner: AR Collector (daily); AR Supervisor (escalation); Finance Manager (legal escalation)
fields.Participants: AR Collector, AR Supervisor, Finance Manager, Sales Rep, Sales Manager, Controller, Legal, Collection Agency
fields.Trigger: Trade or corporate account customer exceeds invoice payment terms (Net 30 or Net 60–90); or monthly scheduled collection review cycle
fields.Volume: ~5,400 active AR accounts (5,200 trade + 200 corporate); ~3,500 AR invoices/month; ~30–40% of accounts typically carrying an overdue balance at any time

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "accounts grouped by aging bucket" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "logs contact attempt, customer response, and committed payment date in system" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-escalate of "escalates to AR Supervisor" (replaces manual Step 3).
Background: W8 covers AR processing — invoice generation, credit limit enforcement, and credit memo handling. W81 covers bad debt provisioning, write-off, and recovery. However, the active collection workflow between an invoice becoming overdue and reaching bad debt write-off is not detailed. At ~5,400 B2B accounts carrying ~40% of company revenue (~PHP 24.9B/year: 30% trade + 10% corporate per §9.1), effective collections directly impact cash flow and working capital. Philippine collections practice involves specific legal requirements (demand letters, BIR documentation) and cultural considerations (relationship-based collection approach). This workflow bridges W8 (AR processing) and W81 (bad debt write-off).
Controls: - CTL-286 (ensure controlled execution — Credit Application & Scoring (PA-16.1).)
- operational: for BIR-compliant bad debt write-off (W81)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Collection fatigue and staff burnout**: making daily collection calls to ~1,500–2,000 overdue accounts is repetitive and emotionally draining; AR Collectors may become desensitized to aging escalation, processing calls mechanically without effective negotiation, leading to declining collection effectiveness over time

- **Sales Rep resistance to collection collaboration**: Sales Reps are compensated on sales volume, not collections; when asked to participate in joint collection calls (step 3), they may resist straining customer relationships; without management enforcement, the Sales Rep collaboration tier of the collection process is inconsistently executed

- **Demand letter compliance for BIR documentation**: formal demand letters sent via registered mail with return card (steps 4–5) are required for BIR-compliant bad debt write-off (W81); if registered mail documentation is not properly filed and retained, the write-off may be disallowed during BIR examination

- **Credit hold override pressure during peak season**: blocking sales to overdue accounts during peak retail season (October–December) generates intense internal pressure from Sales Reps and Store Managers; Finance Manager override approvals may become rubber-stamped under pressure, undermining the credit hold as a collection tool

- **External collection agency performance variability**: licensed collection agencies in the Philippines vary widely in effectiveness; some focus on easy accounts while ignoring difficult ones, and contingency fee structures may incentivize quick settlements at significant discounts rather than full recovery
Staffing Implication: - **2–3 AR Collectors** (within the existing ~46-person Finance team per profile §3.3): ~5,400 active accounts with ~30–40% overdue at any time = ~1,500–2,000 accounts requiring active collection management. At ~15 min average per account per month = ~375–500 hours/month. With 2–3 collectors that's ~150–250 hours each/month ≈ ~7–11 hours/day. This is a full-time role for 2–3 staff. Current AR team can absorb with dedicated collectors.
- **AR Supervisor**: adds ~1 hour/week for team meeting + ~2 hours/month for performance reporting + escalation handling. Absorbed within existing AR Supervisor role.
- **No incremental headcount.**
System Touchpoints: - Automated daily AR aging report with customer contact details, Sales Rep assignment, and collection status (W108.1)
- Automated payment reminders via email/SMS at configurable intervals (W108.2)
- Collection activity logging: contact attempts, customer responses, committed payment dates, dispute notes (W108.2–3)
- Payment term extension request workflow with AR Supervisor approval (W108.3c)
- Credit hold automation: system places hold at 61 days overdue; manual override per CTL-05 (W108.4b)
- Payment plan creation and compliance monitoring with auto-escalation on missed installments (W108.4d)
- Demand letter generation with registered mail tracking (W108.4a, W108.5a)
- Collection agency engagement and performance tracking (W108.7)
- Monthly collection performance dashboard: DSO, CEI, aging trend, write-off rate (W108.9)

- Integration with W7 (AP — collection agency fee processing), W8 (AR — invoice aging, credit memos, credit holds), W24 (credit application — credit limit review triggered by collection history), W58 (corporate accounts — project billing collection), W81 (bad debt write-off — accounts reaching write-off threshold), W84 (customer account reactivation — written-off accounts)
Time Estimate: - Daily overdue identification: automated
- 1–30 day overdue soft collection (calls/emails): ~10–15 min/account × ~800 accounts = ~133–200 hours/month
- 31–60 day overdue active collection: ~20 min/account × ~400 accounts = ~133 hours/month
- 61–90 day overdue escalation (demand letters, credit holds): ~30 min/account × ~150 accounts = ~75 hours/month
- 91–180 day overdue legal escalation: ~1 hour/account × ~50 accounts = ~50 hours/month
- 181+ day write-off/agency coordination: ~30 min/account review × ~20 accounts = ~10 hours/month
- Weekly collection team meeting: ~1 hour/week
- Monthly collection performance reporting: ~2 hours/month
- Quarterly credit review inputs: absorbed in W24 cycle
- Total collection effort: ~400–570 hours/month across 2–3 AR Collectors (~150–190 hours each/month = ~7–9 hours/day)

steps.activity: **Daily overdue identification**: System generates daily AR aging report with overdue accounts grouped by aging bucket: Current, 1–30 days overdue, 31–60 days, 61–90 days, 91–180 days, 181+ days; each account shows: customer name, account number, total overdue amount, oldest invoice date, assigned Sales Rep, last payment date, and last contact date

**1–30 days overdue (soft collection)**: (a) System sends automated payment reminder via email/SMS on day 1 past due and day 15 past due with outstanding invoice details and payment instructions; (b) AR Collector reviews accounts > 15 days overdue; calls customer contact to confirm receipt of invoice and understand payment timeline; (c) AR Collector logs contact attempt, customer response, and committed payment date in system; (d) if customer disputes invoice: AR Collector coordinates with Sales Rep and Billing to resolve dispute within 5 business days

**31–60 days overdue (active collection)**: (a) AR Collector makes weekly follow-up call/email per account; (b) AR Collector and assigned Sales Rep make joint call to customer (Sales Rep relationship leverage); (c) if customer acknowledges debt but requests extension: AR Collector processes payment term extension request with AR Supervisor approval (maximum 30-day extension, one-time per invoice); (d) if customer is unresponsive after 3 contact attempts: system flags account as "Unresponsive" and escalates to AR Supervisor

**61–90 days overdue (escalation)**: (a) AR Supervisor sends formal demand letter (first demand) via registered mail with return card — includes outstanding amount, invoice references, payment demand within 15 days, and notice of potential credit hold; (b) system places account on **credit hold** — new orders blocked until overdue balance resolved; credit hold override per CTL-05 requires Finance Manager approval; (c) AR Supervisor contacts customer's management (not just accounts payable contact) to negotiate payment plan; (d) if customer agrees to payment plan: AR Supervisor records plan in system with installment dates and amounts; system monitors compliance and auto-escalates if any installment missed

**91–180 days overdue (legal escalation)**: (a) Finance Manager sends second demand letter via registered mail with notice of potential legal action; (b) Finance Manager and Sales Manager jointly evaluate account: (i) is the customer still active (recent orders, store visits)?, (ii) is there a legitimate dispute?, (iii) is the business still operating?, (iv) what is the total exposure including unbilled orders?; (c) for active customers with temporary cash flow issues: Finance Manager may approve structured payment plan (maximum 6 months) with personal guarantee or post-dated checks (received and warehoused per W1380); (d) for unresponsive or unwilling customers: Finance Manager escalates to Legal for legal demand letter (third and final demand per Philippine legal practice); (e) Legal reviews account documentation (invoices, delivery receipts signed by customer, demand letters sent, contact logs) and issues final demand letter; (f) system reclassifies receivable to "Litigation" status

**181+ days overdue (external collection / write-off)**: (a) Controller reviews all accounts in 181+ day bucket monthly; (b) for accounts with total exposure > PHP 200,000: Controller recommends engagement of external collection agency per W62 service contract; (c) for accounts where Legal confirms no viable recovery path: Controller initiates bad debt write-off per W81 with supporting documentation (demand letters, contact logs, Legal opinion, agency report); (d) for accounts where customer has partially paid and committed to remaining balance: AR Supervisor monitors payment plan compliance; (e) system maintains full collection history per account for future credit decisions

**Collection agency coordination**: (a) Finance Manager engages licensed collection agency per W62 non-PO contract; (b) AR Supervisor provides agency with complete account documentation package; (c) agency operates on contingency fee basis (typically 10–20% of recovered amount); (d) AR Supervisor monitors agency performance monthly; (e) recovered amounts posted by AR Collector against customer's outstanding balance; (f) agency fees invoiced and processed per W7

**Weekly collection review**: AR Supervisor conducts weekly collection team meeting: (a) review accounts entering new aging buckets, (b) track contact completion rates (target: 100% of accounts contacted within SLA), (c) review payment plan compliance, (d) assign escalated accounts to collectors, (e) identify accounts requiring Sales Rep intervention

**Monthly collection performance reporting**: AR Supervisor prepares monthly collection performance report for Controller and CFO: (a) total AR aging by bucket and trend, (b) days sales outstanding (DSO) — target: < 45 days, (c) collection effectiveness index (CEI) — target: ≥ 85%, (d) bad debt write-off rate as % of revenue — target: < 0.3%, (e) accounts on credit hold — count and value, (f) payment plan portfolio — total value, compliance rate, (g) top 20 overdue accounts by value with status and action plan, (h) Sales Rep territory collection performance comparison

**Quarterly credit review trigger**: Accounts that reached 61+ days overdue during the quarter are flagged for credit limit review in the next quarterly credit review cycle per W24; AR Supervisor provides collection history and recommendation (maintain limit, reduce limit, convert to COD-only, or close account) to Credit Committee

fields.Participants: Store Manager, Lead Cashier, Armoured Car Vendor, Treasury Analyst
fields.Trigger: Daily store cash accumulation exceeds threshold; scheduled armoured car pickup
fields.Volume: ~PHP 350K/day average cash per store (42% of ~PHP 5B monthly retail sales ÷ 200 stores ÷ 30 days)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "count" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "logs seal numbers" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based authorization of "authorized list" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-286 (ensure controlled execution — Credit Application & Scoring (PA-16.1).)
- operational: periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cash shrinkage at high-volume stores**: top-performing Metro Manila stores may handle PHP 5M+ daily cash; even a 0.1% shortage rate equals PHP 5,000/day per store; without real-time variance alerting, cumulative losses across 200 stores can reach PHP 30M+/year before detection

- **CIT vendor reliability in provincial areas**: armored car service coverage is inconsistent outside Metro Manila, Cebu, and Davao; provincial stores may rely on next-day bank branch deposits, increasing overnight cash holding risk and exposure to robbery during holidays and peak seasons

- **Guard authentication fraud risk**: fake or compromised armored car guards are a known risk in the Philippines; the authorized guard/vehicle whitelist (step 3) must be updated in real-time when CIT vendor rotates personnel, which smaller vendors do frequently and with poor notification discipline; mitigated by periodic reconciliation against source documents

- **Reconciliation bottleneck**: Treasury Analyst spends ~2 hours/day matching 200 store deposits; if CIT vendor delays the bank credit report (step 6), reconciliation backlog cascades into W30 daily cash position inaccuracy, affecting cash sweep timing and inter-entity transfer decisions
Staffing Implication: - **Treasury Analysts (2)**: CIT reconciliation adds ~2–4 hours/day to the Treasury team's daily workload; with 200 stores generating daily deposit reconciliation items, this is a significant portion of the Treasury Analyst's day; during peak reconciliation backlogs, a second analyst may be needed to maintain W30 cash position accuracy

- **Store Managers (200)**: daily CIT cash consolidation and handover adds ~40 min to each Store Manager's closing routine; absorbed within W5F store closing procedures but contributes to overtime risk at high-volume stores

- **No incremental headcount**: the Treasury team absorbs CIT reconciliation as a core daily responsibility; however, if store count grows beyond ~250, a dedicated Cash Operations Analyst may be needed
System Touchpoints: - POS EOD / Z-report integration
- Serialized CIT bag/seal tracking
- Guard/Vehicle authorization whitelist
- Bank credit file auto-matching (W30)
- Shortage/Overage exception reporting
Time Estimate: - Per-store daily cash consolidation and bagging: ~40 min/store/day (Lead Cashier + Store Manager)
- Pickup verification and handover: ~10 min/store/day
- System posting: automated
- Daily reconciliation (Treasury Analyst): ~2 hours/day for 200 stores
- Variance investigation: ~30 min/variance × ~10–20 variances/day = ~5–10 hours/day
- Total CIT effort: ~2 hours/day Treasury + ~50 min/day per store (200 stores × Store Manager/Lead Cashier)

steps.activity: **Cash Consolidation**: Lead Cashier performs EOD cash count; reconciles with POS Z-reports (W5F)
**Secure Bagging**: Reconciled cash placed in tamper-evident CIT bags with serialized seals; system logs seal numbers
**Pickup Verification**: Armoured car arrives; Store Manager verifies guard IDs and vehicle number against authorized list
**Handover**: Guard scans CIT bags; Store Manager and Guard sign electronic/physical manifest; copy stored in ERP
**System Posting**: Store Manager marks cash as "In-Transit to Bank"; ERP reduces Store Cash account, increases CIT account
**Bank Acknowledgment**: Bank/CIT vendor processes cash; sends daily credit report
**Reconciliation**: Treasury Analyst matches Bank Credit to Store CIT record; investigates variances > PHP 100

fields.Frequency: Continuous automated monitoring (24/7); monthly portfolio review; quarterly credit policy review
fields.Participants: Credit Analyst, AR Supervisor, Credit Manager, Finance Manager (I), Sales Manager (C for B2B relationship)
fields.Trigger: Continuous monitoring via automated credit scoring engine; monthly credit portfolio review meeting
fields.Volume: ~5,200 trade accounts and ~200 corporate accounts monitored continuously; ~50–100 automated alerts per month requiring review

workflows.name: Customer Credit Monitoring & Automated Alert Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "check history per W1381 — any instance in last 12 months" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-alert of "Alert generation — configurable thresholds trigger tiered alerts" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "reviews daily alert dashboard" (replaces manual Step 3).
Background: W24 covers the initial trade/corporate credit application and approval process. W328 covers annual credit limit periodic review. W108 covers customer credit collection and escalation for overdue accounts. W8 covers accounts receivable processing. W229 covers B2B credit limit exception and escalation. However, no workflow covers ongoing continuous credit monitoring with automated alerts — the real-time surveillance of customer credit health indicators including: payment pattern changes, credit utilization spikes, overdue aging trends, external credit deterioration signals, and industry/market risk factors. For a company with ~5,400 B2B accounts generating ~40% of revenue (PHP ~24.9B annually, per W108 and §9.1), proactive credit monitoring is essential to minimize bad debt exposure while supporting sales growth.
Controls: - CTL-286 (ensure controlled execution — Credit Application & Scoring (PA-16.1).)

- operational: conservative initial credit limits per W24 and proactive monitoring; operational: relying primarily on internal payment behavior data; operational: Sales Manager relationship context (step 9) before taking credit action
Pain Points / Risks: - Philippine construction industry is highly fragmented with many small contractors who have limited financial transparency — credit assessments rely heavily on trade references and payment history rather than formal financial statements; mitigated by conservative initial credit limits per W24 and proactive monitoring

- External credit bureau data (TransUnion, CIBI) may be incomplete for provincial B2B customers — many small contractors and developers outside Metro Manila do not have robust credit bureau profiles; mitigated by relying primarily on internal payment behavior data

- Construction project payment delays cascade from developer to contractor to supplier — customer's late payment may reflect upstream project delay rather than customer financial distress; mitigated by Sales Manager relationship context (step 9) before taking credit action

- Political connections may influence credit decisions creating governance risk — large B2B accounts with political affiliations may pressure for favorable credit terms; mitigated by formal credit action approval workflow (step 7) and monthly portfolio review with Finance Manager and CFO visibility
Staffing Implication: - Covered by existing Credit Manager, Credit Analyst, and AR Supervisor; no incremental headcount needed.
- ~40–50 person-hours/month distributed across credit monitoring team.
- Sales Manager involvement (~30–60 min per Red alert) absorbed within existing B2B relationship management duties.
System Touchpoints: - Credit monitoring and automated alert module with configurable thresholds (FIN-044)
- AR for B2B — account data source for credit health indicators (FIN-005, W8)
- Bad debt provisioning — monitoring feed for provision adequacy review (FIN-022, W81)
- Credit application — initial assessment baseline (W24)
- AR processing — transaction data source (W8)
- Credit collection — escalation partner for overdue accounts (W108)
- Credit limit exception — exception handling partner (W229)
- Credit limit periodic review — annual review partner (W328)
- Bounced check recovery — NSF signal source (W1381)
- Customer master data — credit action update target (W253)
Time Estimate: ~1–2 hours daily for alert review (Credit Analyst). Monthly portfolio review: 2–3 hours. Quarterly policy review: 4 hours. Annual calibration: 1 week. Total: ~40–50 person-hours/month. Absorbed by Credit Analyst, Credit Manager, and AR Supervisor within existing FTEs.

steps.activity: Credit scoring engine continuously monitors credit portfolio using configured rules: (a) payment aging trends — rolling 6-month average days-to-pay vs. prior 6-month period; (b) credit utilization % — current outstanding balance / approved credit limit; (c) average days-to-pay trend — acceleration or deceleration; (d) NSF/bounced check history per W1381 — any instance in last 12 months; (e) order-to-invoice ratio — significant drops may indicate customer financial distress (reducing purchases); (f) external signals — credit bureau updates (TransUnion, CIBI) if enrolled

Alert generation — configurable thresholds trigger tiered alerts: (a) **Amber alert** (watch list): credit utilization >75%, average days-to-pay increased by >10 days vs. rolling average, first bounced check, order volume drop >30% vs. rolling average; (b) **Red alert** (action required): credit utilization >90%, any invoice >60 days overdue, second bounced check within 12 months, external credit bureau deterioration, customer under litigation or insolvency filing; alerts queued in Credit Analyst dashboard with priority ranking

Credit Analyst reviews daily alert dashboard: (a) new alerts generated in last 24 hours; (b) aging of unreviewed alerts (SLA: Amber reviewed within 3 business days, Red reviewed within 1 business day); (c) accounts with multiple concurrent alerts (indicates compounding risk); (d) accounts transitioning from Amber to Red (deterioration trajectory)

For Amber alerts: Credit Analyst conducts preliminary review — (a) pull full payment history for last 12 months; (b) assess if seasonal pattern (construction industry seasonal slowdown June–September during rainy season) or genuine deterioration; (c) check recent payment notes per W108 collection records; (d) review Sales Manager relationship notes; (e) if seasonal or explainable anomaly → no action, add monitoring note, revisit if trend continues for 2 consecutive months; (f) if unexplained deterioration → upgrade to enhanced monitoring with weekly check-in

For Red alerts: Credit Analyst conducts immediate comprehensive review — (a) full account history: all invoices, payments, credits, disputes for last 24 months; (b) collection notes per W108 — last contact date, promised payment dates, dispute status; (c) bounced check details per W1381 — amounts, dates, resolution status; (d) order book: open orders and unshipped SOs that would increase exposure; (e) B2B relationship context: discuss with Sales Manager — is customer experiencing project delay, market downturn, or one-time issue?

Credit Analyst recommends action based on review: (a) **Temporary credit hold** — block new sales orders pending payment of overdue amount (system blocks SO creation per W24 authorization matrix); (b) **Credit limit reduction** — formal notification to customer, reduce limit to current outstanding + 20% buffer; (c) **Payment term tightening** — change from Net 60 to Net 30, or Net 30 to COD; (d) **Cash-on-delivery conversion** — remove credit terms entirely, all future transactions COD; (e) **No action** — false alarm, seasonal pattern, or customer has provided satisfactory explanation with committed payment plan

Credit Manager approves recommended action: (a) credit hold and credit limit changes require Credit Manager approval per W24 authorization matrix; (b) payment term changes require Credit Manager approval with Finance Manager notification; (c) COD conversion requires Credit Manager approval with Sales Manager acknowledgment; (d) Credit Manager reviews recommendation, supporting analysis, and Sales Manager input before decision

System implements approved credit action: (a) update customer master per W253 — credit status, credit limit, payment terms; (b) if credit hold applied: system blocks new sales orders for customer, notifies Sales Manager and assigned Sales Representative, generates hold notification for customer service; (c) generate formal customer notification letter (credit limit change, term change, or COD notification) — reviewed by AR Supervisor for tone and accuracy before sending; (d) all changes logged in credit action audit trail

Customer outreach: (a) Sales Manager contacts customer for relationship management — discusses business situation, conveys credit action as temporary measure, explores payment plan or partial payment arrangement; (b) AR Supervisor contacts customer for payment discussion — presents overdue balance details, negotiates payment commitment date, documents agreement in collection notes per W108; (c) if customer provides payment commitment: Credit Analyst monitors follow-through, escalates missed commitment to Credit Manager within 2 business days

Monthly credit portfolio review meeting: Credit Manager, Finance Manager, and Sales Manager review — (a) top 20 exposures by outstanding balance with risk rating; (b) portfolio aging distribution (current, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+ days) vs. prior month; (c) provision adequacy per W81 — compare actual loss experience to provision rates; (d) alert effectiveness metrics — alerts generated vs. actions taken vs. false positives; (e) policy compliance — accounts exceeding credit limit without approval, credit holds overridden; (f) bad debt forecast for next quarter
steps.r: Credit Manager / Finance Manager / Sales Manager

steps.activity: Quarterly credit policy review: Credit Manager assesses — (a) alert threshold effectiveness: review Amber-to-Red transition rate, false positive rate, missed deterioration (accounts that defaulted without triggering alert); (b) recommend threshold adjustments to optimize detection vs. false positive balance; (c) update scoring model weights based on latest 12 months of default data; (d) review industry/market risk factors — construction sector outlook, government infrastructure spending, interest rate environment

Annual credit scoring model calibration: Credit Analyst recalibrates scoring model using actual default data — (a) analyze defaulted accounts (written off per W81) vs. performing accounts to identify predictive factors; (b) update weighting of risk factors (utilization, aging, bounced checks, external scores); (c) back-test revised model against historical data; (d) present calibration results to Finance Manager for approval; (e) deploy updated model parameters to production

fields.Frequency: Monthly operational review; quarterly strategic review
fields.Participants: Credit Analyst, Collection Officer, Finance Manager, Head of Trade / Account Management
fields.Volume: ~5,200 trade accounts + ~200 corporate accounts; ~PHP 1.5–2.0B total AR portfolio (per W1300)

workflows.name: Customer Credit Portfolio Periodic Review & Collection Strategy

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "accounts as % of total AR" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews portfolio health metrics vs." (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "checks per W1381, accounts with declining order frequency" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-286 (ensure controlled execution — Credit Application & Scoring (PA-16.1).)
- operational: Credit Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - Construction sector concentration risk; government account long payment cycles; economic downturn impact on trade customer solvency; provision adequacy judgment
Staffing Implication: - Credit Manager: ~1 day/month + 2 days/quarter. Absorbed within existing role.
System Touchpoints: - AR aging module
- Credit scoring engine
- Collection management system
- Customer master
- GL provision module
Time Estimate: - Monthly: 1 day; quarterly strategic: 2 days

steps.activity: System generates credit portfolio dashboard: total AR, aging distribution, DSO, bad debt provision, credit utilization rate, portfolio concentration (top 20 accounts as % of total AR)
Credit Manager reviews portfolio health metrics vs. policy targets: DSO target ≤ 45 days, 90+ aging ≤ 8%, annual bad debt ≤ 0.5% of revenue

Credit Analyst identifies accounts requiring individual review: accounts approaching credit limit (> 85% utilization), accounts with aging > 60 days, accounts with recent bounced checks per W1381, accounts with declining order frequency
Collection Officer reviews active collection actions per W108: promise-to-pay compliance, legal collection status, write-off candidates per W81

Credit Manager develops collection strategy adjustments: tighten terms for high-risk segments, offer early payment incentives for 90+ accounts, escalate top 20 overdue accounts to Head of Trade / Account Management for relationship intervention

Monthly: Credit Manager produces portfolio report for Finance Manager; Quarterly: strategic review with Head of Trade / Account Management and CFO including portfolio risk assessment, industry sector analysis (construction, government, developer), and provision adequacy review
Credit Manager updates credit policy parameters based on portfolio review findings (risk scoring model thresholds, sector limits, automatic hold triggers)

fields.Participants: Finance Manager, Tax Accountant, External Auditor, CFO, VP Legal
fields.Trigger: Discovery of material error in posted financial statements; external auditor adjustment during annual audit per W351; BIR assessment requiring correction of prior-period tax filing; management-initiated correction of accounting policy misapplication

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "review, internal audit per W121, reconciliation per W636" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "documenting error, impact, and proposed correction" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approved restatement plan documented with authorization signatures" (replaces manual Step 3).
Background: When a material error is discovered in previously issued financial statements — whether from an accounting policy misapplication, calculation error, omission, or fraud — PFRS/PAS 8 requires correction with retrospective application. For a PHP 62.3B revenue company with 5 legal entities and BIR/SEC reporting obligations, restatements require careful documentation, multi-entity impact assessment, and coordinated regulatory communication. This workflow complements W9A (month-end close) and W9B (year-end close) by addressing the rare but critical scenario of correcting already-reported financials.
Controls: - CTL-286 (ensure controlled execution — Credit Application & Scoring (PA-16.1).)
- operational: Controller review and approval gate; operational: periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **BIR penalty exposure**: restatements affecting tax filings trigger BIR penalties (compromise penalty of 25% of deficiency tax per NIRC); voluntary disclosure before BIR discovery mitigates penalty severity
- **SEC filing deadlines**: amended AFS must be filed within SEC-prescribed periods; late filing penalties and potential SEC scrutiny of the company's financial reporting controls

- **Audit opinion impact**: material restatements may result in external auditor issuing qualified opinion or emphasis of matter paragraph, affecting lender confidence and debt covenant compliance per W319

- **Multi-entity cascading effects**: an error in one entity may cascade through IC eliminations per W234, transfer pricing per W235, and consolidation per W9A, requiring corrections across all 5 entities
- **Internal morale and credibility**: financial restatements erode management's credibility with the board and external stakeholders; transparent communication is essential but uncomfortable
Staffing Implication: Ad-hoc (rare). Each material restatement requires 2-4 days of concentrated effort from Controller, Finance Manager, and Tax Accountant. No incremental headcount; absorbed by existing finance team with reprioritization of routine tasks. External auditor involvement per W351 adds 2-4 hours of coordination per restatement.
System Touchpoints: - GL module with prior-period adjustment posting capability and retroactive effect
- Multi-entity posting with automated IC adjustment per W14
- Audit trail with "Restatement" flag for enhanced traceability
- Period-end journal entry review workflow per W638
- Consolidated financial statement re-generation per W9A
- BIR eFPS amended return filing per W260
- SEC reportorial requirements filing per W481
- Financial controls testing module per W637
Time Estimate: **Total**: 3-5 business days per material restatement (2-4 hours identification + 4-8 hours scoping + 1-2 hours approval + 4-8 hours journal entries + 2-4 hours review + 1-2 days re-issuance + 2-4 hours auditor communication + 4-8 hours RCA). Timeline extends if multiple entities or periods are affected.

steps.activity: **Error identification and assessment**: (a) source identifies error: internal discovery (month-end review, internal audit per W121, reconciliation per W636), external auditor per W351, or BIR assessment per W77; (b) Controller performs materiality assessment: quantify financial impact on each affected entity and consolidated group; (c) determine if error is material (requires restatement) or immaterial (prospectively corrected per W638); (d) if material: escalate to CFO with written assessment

**Restatement scoping**: Controller and Finance Manager define scope: (a) identify all affected periods (current year, prior years); (b) identify all affected entities (1-5 entities depending on error); (c) map impact to: income statement lines, balance sheet accounts, cash flow items, equity changes; (d) assess tax impact: VAT, income tax, withholding tax, local business tax; (e) identify downstream impacts: budget variance per W26, management reporting per W35, KPI calculations per W665; (f) prepare restatement memo documenting error, impact, and proposed correction

**CFO and Audit Committee approval**: (a) CFO reviews restatement memo; (b) if error affects consolidated financial statements: present to Audit Committee for approval before execution; (c) if error affects BIR filings: engage VP Legal for assessment of penalty exposure and voluntary disclosure strategy; (d) approved restatement plan documented with authorization signatures

**Journal entry preparation**: Tax Accountant / Finance Manager prepares correcting entries: (a) prior-year adjustments posted to retained earnings (per PFRS/PAS 8 retrospective application); (b) current-year corrections posted to affected accounts with detailed supporting schedules; (c) multi-entity entries: IC adjustments if error affected intercompany transactions per W14; (d) tax adjustments: correcting entries for VAT, income tax, withholding tax as needed; (e) all entries reviewed by Controller before posting

**Period-end journal entry review per W638**: correcting entries submitted through W638 review and approval process with enhanced scrutiny: (a) Controller reviews all restatement journal entries; (b) dual approval required: Controller + CFO; (c) entries posted with special "Restatement" flag in audit trail; (d) system generates restatement-specific audit log

**Financial statement revision and re-issuance**: (a) revise affected financial statements for all impacted periods; (b) update comparative figures (prior year columns) per PFRS/PAS 8; (c) prepare revised notes to financial statements with restatement disclosure; (d) if previously filed with SEC: prepare and file amended AFS per W481; (e) if previously filed with BIR: prepare and file amended tax returns per W260; (f) re-issue internal management reports for affected periods per W35

**External auditor communication**: (a) notify external auditor of restatement per W351 coordination; (b) provide restatement memo, supporting schedules, and corrected financial statements; (c) external auditor assesses restatement impact on their audit opinion; (d) if restatement affects current-year audit: adjust audit plan and timeline; (e) obtain external auditor sign-off on restated figures

**Root cause analysis and controls remediation**: (a) Controller conducts RCA to determine how the error occurred and why it was not detected; (b) identify control failures: preventive, detective, or monitoring; (c) implement remediation: process changes, system validations, additional review steps; (d) update financial controls testing per W637; (e) document lessons learned and communicate to finance team

steps.activity: Receive credit application — Sales Representative or customer submits application: (a) company/legal entity details (SEC/DTI registration), (b) trade references (3 minimum), (c) bank references, (d) financial statements (audited if available), (e) authorized signatories, (f) requested credit limit and terms, (g) BIR TIN, (h) business permit

Verify applicant documentation — validate: (a) SEC/DTI registration via online verification, (b) BIR TIN via the BIR TIN Validation System / eRegistration, (c) Mayor's permit validity, (d) trade reference legitimacy (call each reference), (e) bank reference verification, (f) financial statement reasonableness; flag discrepancies

Conduct credit scoring — apply internal credit scoring model: (a) years in business (> 5 years: positive), (b) industry risk (construction: moderate), (c) financial ratios (current ratio, debt-to-equity, net margin), (d) trade reference feedback, (e) banking relationship, (f) geographic risk (Mindanao vs. Luzon), (g) BuildRight relationship history (if existing cash customer); calculate composite score (0–100)

Determine credit recommendation — based on score: (a) Score ≥ 75: approve at requested limit or 80% of requested, (b) Score 50–74: approve at reduced limit (50% of requested) with shorter terms (15 days vs. 30), (c) Score 30–49: approve with COD or secured terms (post-dated checks per W1380), (d) Score < 30: decline with counter-offer for cash terms only

Credit approval authorization per W24's canonical matrix — (a) ≤ PHP 200,000: AR Supervisor, (b) PHP 200,001–1,000,000: Finance Manager, (c) > PHP 1,000,000: Credit Committee (CFO + Finance Manager + AR Supervisor)

Notify customer and Sales Representative — communicate credit decision: approved (with limit, terms, and conditions), conditionally approved (with counter-offer), or declined (with reason and reapplication eligibility); send credit agreement for signature

Set up customer in AR module — create customer account with: approved credit limit, payment terms (net 15/30/45/60), credit score, review date (6 months for new accounts), authorized signatories, and billing address; activate for credit sales

steps.activity: Identify accounts due for review — system generates review list based on: (a) scheduled review date, (b) limit utilization > 85% for 3 consecutive months, (c) payment delinquency (any invoice > 30 days past due), (d) customer request for increase, (e) significant order exceeding current limit

Compile review data package — for each account: (a) 12-month payment history, (b) average days-to-pay, (c) credit utilization trend, (d) order frequency and value trend, (e) any disputes or credit memos, (f) updated financial information (if available), (g) industry/economic conditions

Assess creditworthiness update — recalculate credit score with current data: (a) payment behavior change (improving or deteriorating), (b) order volume trend, (c) outstanding AR aging, (d) any collection activity, (e) external factors (construction industry outlook, regional economic conditions)

Determine credit limit recommendation — options: (a) Maintain current limit, (b) Increase (if utilization consistently high and payment is timely — typically 20–50% increase), (c) Decrease (if payment deterioration — typically to 50–75% of current), (d) Suspend credit (convert to cash terms), (e) Close account (if inactive > 12 months or severe default)

Obtain approval — per W24's canonical matrix (≤ PHP 200K: AR Supervisor; PHP 200K–1M: Finance Manager; > PHP 1M: Credit Committee); for limit decreases, Credit Manager can approve all; for suspensions, Finance Controller approval required

Communicate decision — notify Sales Representative and customer of any limit change; for decreases: explain reason and remediation path; for increases: confirm new terms; for suspensions: coordinate transition to cash terms
Update AR module — adjust credit limit, update review date, record review notes; if suspended: apply credit hold (W888)

steps.activity: System detects credit hold trigger — automated checks: (a) new order would exceed credit limit, (b) invoice > 30 days past due (for Net 30), (c) invoice > 45 days (for Net 45), (d) invoice > 60 days (for Net 60), (e) NSF/bounced check from customer; order automatically blocked in order processing

Review and validate hold — Credit Analyst reviews: (a) verify overdue amount and invoice details, (b) check for payments in transit (customer may have paid but not yet posted), (c) review for disputed invoices (hold should not apply to disputed amounts), (d) check for partial payments that may release hold

Escalation for chronic offenders — accounts with > 3 holds in rolling 90 days flagged for Credit Manager review: consider limit reduction (W887) or terms modification; notify Finance Controller
Daily credit hold report — generate report: total accounts on hold, total blocked order value, aging of holds, release rate, and chronic offender list; distribute to Credit Manager and COO

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "account volume and default rate" (replaces manual Step 1).

Pain Points / Risks: - Credit scoring model may not capture construction industry cyclicality — sector-specific factors needed

steps.activity: Compile portfolio performance data — extract from trailing 12 months: (a) total credit sales, (b) total collections, (c) bad debt write-offs, (d) DSO trend, (e) aging distribution, (f) credit limit utilization, (g) credit score distribution, (h) new account volume and default rate

Analyze portfolio risk concentration — assess: (a) top 20 accounts as % of total AR (concentration risk), (b) geographic concentration, (c) industry concentration (construction, manufacturing, government), (d) terms distribution, (e) aging migration (accounts moving to higher risk buckets)

Validate credit scoring model — compare predicted default rates (by score band) to actual default/write-off rates: (a) score ≥ 75: actual default rate vs. expected (< 1%), (b) score 50–74: actual vs. expected (1–3%), (c) score < 50: actual vs. expected (> 3%); recalibrate model if deviation > 20%

Conduct top 200 account deep-dive — for top accounts by exposure: (a) review credit score and payment trend, (b) assess industry and project risk, (c) evaluate limit adequacy, (d) identify early warning indicators (slowing payments, reduced order frequency), (e) recommend action (maintain, increase, decrease, suspend)

Calculate portfolio expected loss — apply probability of default (PD) and loss given default (LGD) by score band to current portfolio: (a) expected loss = Σ (exposure × PD × LGD), (b) compare to allowance for doubtful accounts balance, (c) recommend reserve adjustment if under/over-provisioned

Present portfolio review to the CFO — key findings: (a) portfolio health score, (b) risk concentration concerns, (c) scoring model performance, (d) expected loss vs. reserves, (e) top account recommendations, (f) policy and process improvement proposals

Implement approved changes — update: (a) credit scoring model weights, (b) approval thresholds, (c) collection strategy for high-risk segments, (d) credit policy amendments, (e) allowance for doubtful accounts reserve

workflows.name: Customer Trade Account Credit Limit Periodic Review, Risk Scoring & Adjustment

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Automated risk scoring" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "Segmentation & prioritization" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "check for open disputes or complaints per W41" (replaces manual Step 3).
Background: BuildRight Depot manages ~5,200 active trade AR accounts (Section 10.3) with credit terms of Net 30. Credit limits are set per account based on the initial credit application per W24. However, business conditions change: contractors grow (larger projects, higher credit needs) or shrink (fewer projects, payment difficulties). The credit limit set 12 months ago may no longer be appropriate. Quarterly periodic review ensures: (a) credit limits reflect current risk profile, (b) high-growth accounts can access more credit to buy more from BuildRight, (c) deteriorating accounts are identified early before bad debt per W81, and (d) overall AR portfolio risk is managed within acceptable parameters. Philippine construction industry dynamics (project-based revenue, seasonal fluctuations during rainy season, typhoon impacts) make regular credit review especially important.
Controls: - CTL-286 (ensure controlled execution — Credit Application & Scoring (PA-16.1).)
- operational: Credit & Collections Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Customer relationship tension** — decreasing a credit limit or suspending credit strains the B2B relationship; B2B Account Manager must communicate sensitively while protecting BuildRight's financial exposure
- **Data quality** — risk scoring depends on accurate payment and order data; if AP/AR data is incomplete or delayed per W9A month-end close, scoring is unreliable

- **Approval bottleneck** — high-value credit limit increases require Finance Manager or CFO approval; if these approvers are unavailable, credit limit increases are delayed, potentially constraining sales

- **Seasonal distortion** — rainy season (Jun–Aug) may cause temporary payment delays for contractors whose projects are weather-delayed; scoring must account for seasonality to avoid unnecessary credit tightening
Staffing Implication: - Credit & Collections Manager: ~870–975 hours/quarter for ~1,300 flagged-account reviews (40–45 min each, per the step durations) — shared with the Credit Analyst team. No incremental headcount at the current flagged-subset volume.
System Touchpoints: - W24 credit application & approval for initial credit setup
- W8 AR & credit management for credit hold and override
- W108 customer credit collection & escalation for overdue management
- W81 bad debt provisioning for write-off risk assessment
- W893 credit scorecard for portfolio analysis
- W1240 project follow-up for relationship intelligence
- W41 complaint management for dispute impact on credit
Time Estimate: - Quarterly: ~870–975 hours for the ~1,300 flagged-account reviews (per the step-duration derivation) + ~10 hours for system setup and reporting. Annual: ~3,530–3,940 hours.

steps.activity: **Automated risk scoring**: System calculates updated risk score for each trade account: (a) payment history (on-time %, average days-to-pay, number of late payments in last 6 months); (b) current AR aging (current, 30+, 60+, 90+ days); (c) credit utilization (outstanding balance ÷ credit limit); (d) order frequency and value trend; (e) external data (if available: business registration status, SEC filing updates)

**Segmentation & prioritization**: System segments accounts: (a) increase recommended (utilization >80%, good payment history, growing order trend); (b) maintain (stable metrics, utilization 30–80%); (c) decrease recommended (late payments increasing, utilization >90%, declining order trend); (d) watch list (score dropped significantly, 60+ day aging); (e) immediate review (90+ day aging, overlimit)

**Individual account review**: Credit & Collections Manager reviews flagged accounts (increase/decrease/watch/immediate): (a) review payment history details; (b) review B2B Account Manager notes from W1240 project follow-ups; (c) check for open disputes or complaints per W41; (d) assess business relationship value (annual revenue, strategic importance)

**Credit limit decision**: For each reviewed account: (a) increase: justified by growth and good payment → raise limit (approval per tier: <PHP 500K by Credit Manager, <PHP 2M by Finance Manager, >PHP 2M by CFO); (b) maintain: no change, continue monitoring; (c) decrease: justified by risk → lower limit (communicate to customer proactively via B2B Account Manager); (d) suspend: severe risk → suspend credit, convert to COD per W8

**Customer communication**: B2B Account Manager communicates limit changes to customer: (a) for increases: positive news, reinforces relationship; (b) for decreases: explain reason (payment pattern, portfolio policy), offer path to restoration; (c) for suspension: formal notification, outstanding balance collection plan per W108

**System update**: Update credit limit in ERP: (a) new limit effective immediately; (b) system enforces new limit on future orders; (c) if decrease: system allows existing committed orders to proceed (grandfathered) but blocks new orders exceeding new limit; (d) update credit scorecard per W893

workflows.name: Trade Account Credit Limit Annual Review, Adjustment & Exposure Monitoring

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "review scheduling & data compilation" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "Credit scoring recalculation" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-count of "Credit limit decision" (replaces manual Step 3).
Background: BuildRight Depot extends trade credit to ~5,200 accounts (contractors, builders, interior designers, architects) with combined outstanding AR of ~PHP 1.5–2.0B at any time. Credit terms range from Net 30 (standard trade) to Net 60–90 (corporate projects). Each account has a credit limit set during initial credit scoring per W100. However, trade customer financial health changes over time: (a) a contractor may take on too many projects simultaneously, overleveraging and missing payments to suppliers including BuildRight; (b) a previously stable corporate account may face cash flow problems from delayed government project payments (common in the Philippines — government infrastructure project retainers are released on 60–90 day cycles); (c) construction industry downturns (post-pandemic, typhoon damage to contractor cash flow) affect entire segments. Without systematic annual review, BuildRight may continue extending credit to deteriorating accounts, increasing bad debt exposure. This workflow manages the systematic review, adjustment, and monitoring of trade account credit limits.
Controls: - CTL-286 (ensure controlled execution — Credit Application & Scoring (PA-16.1).)
- operational: Credit & Collections Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Philippine credit bureau limitations** — credit bureau coverage for small contractors and sole proprietorships is sparse; many trade customers have no external credit history, making BuildRight's internal payment history the primary scoring input

- **Sales vs. Credit tension** — Sales Managers want to extend more credit to drive volume; Credit Managers want to limit exposure; CFO must balance growth and risk; mitigated by the Credit & Collections Manager review and approval gate

- **Government project payment delays** — contractors working on government projects face chronic payment delays (90–180 days); these contractors are otherwise good accounts but are consistently past due; a separate scoring adjustment for government-project-dependent contractors may be needed

- **Personal relationship dependency** — many trade accounts are small businesses where the personal financial health of the owner is the primary credit risk; monitoring owner financial changes is difficult without formal financial statement requirements; mitigated by the Credit & Collections Manager review and approval gate
Staffing Implication: - **Credit Analyst**: ~5,200 annual reviews × 20 min avg = ~1,730 hours/year (~1 FTE); absorbed by existing credit team
- **Credit & Collections Manager**: ~6 hours/month on portfolio review + ~10 hours/month on escalated decisions
- **No incremental headcount**
System Touchpoints: - Credit management module — score calculation, limit tracking, tier management
- AR aging module — payment history, aging analysis
- Customer master — credit limit, terms, score, review date
- External credit bureau integration — CIC, TransUnion Philippines data pull
- Approval workflow — tiered approval routing for credit limit changes
- BI dashboard — portfolio exposure, aging trends, concentration analysis
Time Estimate: - Per account review: 20–30 min
- Annual reviews: ~5,200 × 25 min avg = ~2,170 hours
- Portfolio monitoring: ~6 hours/month
- **Total annual: ~2,240 hours (~1.1 FTE)**

steps.activity: **Annual review scheduling & data compilation**: (a) system generates monthly batch of accounts due for annual review (by credit approval anniversary month); (b) Credit Analyst compiles review package per account: (i) payment history over past 12 months (on-time %, average days past due, highest aging bucket reached), (ii) purchase volume trend (increasing, stable, declining), (iii) current outstanding balance vs. credit limit utilization, (iv) number of credit limit increase requests in past 12 months, (v) any returned checks or payment disputes, (vi) external credit bureau data (if available — Philippine credit bureaus like CIC, TransUnion Philippines)

**Credit scoring recalculation**: System recalculates credit score using updated data: (a) payment score (40% weight): on-time payment rate, average days past due, returned check count; (b) volume score (20% weight): purchase volume trend and consistency; (c) utilization score (20% weight): credit limit utilization rate — chronically maxed-out accounts score lower; (d) tenure score (10% weight): years as BuildRight trade customer; (e) external score (10% weight): credit bureau score if available; (f) resulting score maps to credit tier: (i) Platinum (score ≥ 85): credit limit up to PHP 5M, terms Net 60, (ii) Gold (score 70–84): credit limit up to PHP 2M, terms Net 30, (iii) Silver (score 55–69): credit limit up to PHP 500K, terms Net 30, (iv) Bronze (score 40–54): credit limit up to PHP 200K, terms Net 30 with 10% holdback, (v) Probation (score < 40): credit limit reduced to PHP 50K or suspended, COD terms

steps.a: Credit & Collections Manager (or CFO for large increases)
steps.activity: **Credit limit decision**: Credit Analyst reviews score and recommends: (a) maintain current limit and terms, (b) increase limit and/or improve terms (for improving accounts), (c) decrease limit and/or tighten terms (for deteriorating accounts), (d) suspend credit and convert to COD (for severely deteriorating accounts); for limit increases > PHP 1M: Credit & Collections Manager approval required; for limit increases > PHP 3M: CFO approval required; for credit suspension: Credit & Collections Manager approval with Sales Manager notification

**Customer communication**: (a) for credit limit increases: system sends notification to customer with new limit and terms — positive engagement opportunity; (b) for credit limit decreases: Credit Analyst calls customer to explain change, discusses remediation path (e.g., "bring all payments current within 60 days and your score will improve"); (c) for credit suspension: Sales Manager and Credit Analyst meet with customer to discuss: is the account salvageable? can customer provide additional guarantees (personal guarantee of company owner, post-dated checks)?; (d) all decisions documented in ERP credit management module

**Portfolio-level exposure monitoring**: Monthly, Credit & Collections Manager reviews portfolio-level exposure: (a) total AR outstanding vs. portfolio credit limit (total approved limits), (b) aging distribution: current, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+ days, (c) concentration risk: top 20 accounts as % of total AR, (d) industry segment exposure (construction, government projects, interior design, etc.), (e) bad debt provision adequacy: actual write-off rate vs. provision rate, (f) report to CFO with recommendations for portfolio-level action (tighten new credit approvals, increase bad debt provision, engage collection agency for 90+ accounts)
